relations.evidence: ADR 0044 Decision, The breaker: "Per provider, shared by every wrapped agent in the process: MODEL_BREAKER_THRESHOLD consecutive failures (default 5; 0 disables) open it for MODEL_BREAKER_COOLDOWN_MS (default 30 s)". circuitBreaker.ts holds that state for FallbackLlm and FallbackAdapter alike.

ADR 0044 Note (2026-10-07): adapters that yield an error response "set customMetadata['error.retryable'] (and 'error.status') from retry.ts's classification (lib/models/errorResponse.ts)", which is what decides whether a fallback answers.

ADR 0044 Decision: "the compiler wraps the agent's model in FallbackLlm (lib/models/fallback.ts)"; only a retryable provider-side failure before any output redirects; Note (2026-10-07): the rule holds for error responses as well as throws, and only a call that yielded content counts as a success.

ADR 0044 Decision, What redirects: only a provider-side failure that retry.ts classifies retryable, "redirected only if the primary had produced nothing yet"; a 4xx, a canceled turn and a stream that failed midway are never redirected. FallbackAdapter applies these to a failed final's error.retryable and status.

ADR 0024 note (2026-10-07): "Owning the agent loop is no longer deferred. The engine builds its own runtime in stages behind this seam ... see ADR 0045. Items 1 (the seam), 2, 3 and 5 stand; item 4 holds while ADK is a runtime."
relations.note: In part: supersedes the deferral of owning the agent loop and ADK as the lasting runtime; the seam, turn-wide controls, boundary suite and A2A stance stand.

/memory/architecture.md, Stored event shape: "With `--check` it exits 1 when a fixture no longer matches what the runtime writes, which is what a dependency bump that changes the stored shape looks like. `npm run fixtures:sessions:check` runs that check, and CI's test job runs it after the offline suite on both Node versions."
relations.note: The script runs tests/fixtures/sessions/generate.ts --check; the build links scripts only to source modules, so this edge is asserted.

relations.evidence: /operations/parity-harness.md: "`npm run parity` (`scripts/parity_check.ts`) answers one question per provider: does the engine's core work end to end on it? ... A runtime gate is a run of this script, not a manual check."

ADR 0045, decision 4: the stored Event JSON in adk_sessions.events never changes without an ADR; its note (2026-10-07): "The stored Event JSON in item 4 carries an elided tool result's size inside its marker text. trimEventForStorage (lib/session/transcript.ts) now writes that size with en-US digit grouping".

ADR 0048 Consequences: "Lowercase JSON Schema is the one dialect inside the contract. A schema in Gemini's uppercase dialect is converted once, where it enters, instead of by every adapter." contractToolDeclaration and toContractJsonSchema are that conversion.
ADR 0049 §4: "Rows not bound to the conversation replay as ADR 0046 says"; on bound rows the same replay rides under drop_block, closing ADR 0046's named gap for resumed turns.

ADR 0049 §4 and Context: trimEventForStorage elides tool results over 2,000 characters and JSONB reorders keys, so a resumed turn differs from what the model saw; drop_block makes the API drop a changed block instead of failing, and "The session stores do not change."
ADR 0049 §2: "This supersedes ADR 0047's statement that the Claude adapter never reads the effort word: on the adaptive rows it is the only thing it reads."
relations.note: In part: only how the Claude adapter reads the reasoning fields. ADR 0047's key, levels and compiler mapping stand.
